The Encouragement the Sahabah (RA) Gave Towards Dhikr
The Encouragement Hadhrat Umar (RA), Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) and Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) Gave Towards Dhikr

Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Do not preoccupy yourself with discussing people because it is a cause of misfortune. You had rather engage constantly in the Dhikr of Allaah." [^2] Another narration states that Hadhrat Umar (RA) said, "Engage assiduously in the Dhikr of Allaah because it is a cure. At the same time, avoid discussing people because it is a disease." [^3]
Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) said, "Had our hearts been pure, we would never tire with the Dhikr of Allaah." [^4]
Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Mas'ood (RA) said, "Engage abundantly in the Dhikr of Allaah and it matters not if you do not associate with anyone apart from those who can assist you in Dhikr." [^5]
The Encouragement Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) and Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) Gave Towards Dhikr

Hadhrat Salmaan (RA) once said that if a man spends an entire night giving away slave women with fair complexions and another man spends the night reciting the Book of Allaah and engaging in Dhikr, the latter is the better of the two. [^6]

Hadhrat Ahmad bin Habeeb bin Ubayd narrates that a man approached Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) and asked for some advice. Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) said, "Remember Allaah during times of ease and Allaah will remember you during your times of hardship. Whenever you are impressed by anything of this world, consider what it is soon to become." [^7]
blocks.narrator: Hadhrat Ahmad bin Habeeb bin Ubayd

blocks.text: Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) once said, "Shall I not inform you of the best of all deeds, which is most beloved to your Master and will elevate your rank the most? It is better than being killed and killing the enemy in Jihaad and even better than giving Dirhams and Dinaars in charity."
